deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: prompt-bridge-v3 -> route=prompt_route_v3 -> 7% traffic. Deployed by @Arjun at 2059876543
Maya (oncall): I'm getting paged, traffic spike + 5xxs on prompt routing, alert: /v1/prompt route 5xx rate 24% :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): paging: Sev2 - widespread error rate increase on prompt requests, customers seeing failures
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-205987 - High 5xx rate for prompt routing. Severity: S2. Paging oncall Maya. Related services: prompt-router, prompt-bridge-v3, canary controller
Maya (oncall): quick checks: rolling windows show 5xx rate jumped at 2059876550, canary traffic went from 0%->7% around deploy time
Jamie (runtime): on it. linking runbook: /runbooks/prompt-routing-canary-failures. suggest flip circuit-breaker flag for new route to fallback to stable route while we triage
Maya (oncall): agreed. how do we flip?
Arjun (eng-tools): I pushed the canary. Flag is `circuit_breaker_prompt_v3`. CLI to toggle: `ffctl toggle --flag circuit_breaker_prompt_v3 --env prod --on`
Arjun (eng-tools): running it now: ```$ ffctl toggle --flag circuit_breaker_prompt_v3 --env prod --on
> success: circuit_breaker_prompt_v3=ON
```
Maya (oncall): toggled. monitoring metrics...
Li (support): Support seeing escalation on two enterprise customers via intercom, both reporting immediate failures when sending prompts. ETA to customers? we should send a status update if impact persists >15min
Jamie (runtime): after toggle: 5xx rate dropped from 24% -> 2% within 30s, p99 latency for prompt endpoint reduced 1.2s -> 0.35s. canary now effectively short-circuited back to stable route
Maya (oncall): nice. marking mitigation: feature-flag circuit-breaker ON (prompt_route_v3). Incident still open for RCA and rollback plan
Sasha (product): how many requests affected during window? we need an impact summary for stakeholders
Ben (reliability): quick estimate from metrics: ~3.8k requests failed in the 5m window, ~0.04% overall platform traffic. no billing anomalies detected. no data exfiltration suspected
Arjun (eng-tools): logs show: prompt-bridge-v3 returned `500` with message `unknown_model_id` due to a header mismatch when router sent model id `redwood/model-v2` instead of `redwood/model-v2-quant`. looks like the new adapter didn't map legacy ids correctly
Jamie (runtime): confirmed in canary logs. stacktrace snippet: ```2026-03-15T12:15:50Z prompt-bridge-v3 ERROR handler.go:142 mapping error: model id not found -> 500
```
Maya (oncall): ok root cause suspect config mapping regression in adapter. what's next: rollback canary completely, or keep ff circuit-breaker on and patch mapping?
Arjun (eng-tools): rollback would be `kubectl rollout undo deployment/prompt-bridge-v3 -n prod --to-revision=...` but we already stopped traffic via flag. I'd prefer to keep flag ON and push a hotfix adapter mapping ASAP, then test, then unflag
Jamie (runtime): agree, safer to hotfix. create patch branch and a tiny traffic-only test. I'll pair with Arjun
Li (support): I'll draft a 15-min status message for affected customers. suggested copy: "We detected elevated errors on prompt requests and have routed traffic to a stable endpoint. Mitigation in place and engineers are investigating. We will follow up with a timeline"
Sasha (product): please include that this was during a controlled canary rollout and that no customer data was exposed. keep message short
Maya (oncall): assigning owners: Arjun + Jamie for fix, Li for customer comms, Ben for follow-up monitoring. I'll keep incident bridge open.
incident-bot: Handoff requested: next on-call @Ben in 30m. Current oncall Maya -> handing over at 2059876680. Incident remains open
Ben (reliability): taking over in 30, will keep watch. quick ask: please add a runbook note about using circuit_breaker flag for this flow
Arjun (eng-tools): quick repro steps I used to validate mapping locally: ```
# simulate incoming header
curl -X POST https://staging-prompt-bridge/api/generate -H 'X-Model-ID: redwood/model-v2' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# we see 500 with mapping error
```
Jamie (runtime): hotfix PR created: `fix/adapter-id-mapping`. tests: unit + integration against stable model map. deploying to staging now
Maya (oncall): ETA patch to prod?
Jamie (runtime): staging green in 8m, will push to prod with 0-1% canary then unset circuit-breaker after validation. total ~25m from now
Li (support): I'll send initial status now and update after prod patch. tagging CS leads
Sasha (product): add a note for postmortem: tighten canary gating criteria (increase preflight checks for model id mappings) and consider automated flag engagement when 5xx > 5% for >2min
Ben (reliability): +1. also add an alert that watches for sudden mapping-related 500 signatures to auto-suppress canary and page oncall
Maya (oncall): summary for handoff -> Cause: adapter mapping regression in prompt-bridge-v3 introduced by canary; Impact: ~3.8k failed prompt requests during 5m window, mitigated by enabling `circuit_breaker_prompt_v3` which routed traffic to stable endpoint; Next steps: hotfix mapping, staged rollout, update runbook, postmortem.
Maya (oncall): handing incident to Ben now. I'll be available for questions. :wave:
Ben (reliability): got it, taking over. I'll coordinate postmortem and timeline. please drop any logs/links in this thread. :thumbsup:
Arjun (eng-tools): logs & PR link: https://git.redwood/infer/prompt-bridge/pull/482, cloudwatch group: /prod/prompt-bridge-v3, canary controller events: https://console.redwood/canaries/2059876543
incident-bot: Incident INC-205987 mitigated (circuit-breaker engaged). Status: working fix. Please update incident when resolved or rolled back.
Ben (reliability): leaving bridge open until patch verifies in prod and circuit-breaker toggled off safely. will post final resolution and a short timeline once complete.
Maya (oncall): thanks team. closing my active handover.
